review_notes:
I read the whole file and the Mathlib lemma `Complex.IsConservativeOn.eventually_nhds_wedgeIntegral_sub_wedgeIntegral` in Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/HasPrimitives.lean.

Inside the target there are three declarations. The first, `exists_hasDerivAt_eqOn_ball_inter_upperHalfPlane`, is a single argument. The second, the wedge additivity theorem, has two helpers, `integrableHoriz` and `integrableVert`, and the ordinary pieces `hI₁`, `hI₂`, `hrect` and `hI₀`. Each helper is used only in its own proof, and the `rcases` branches inside `integrableVert` are short and routine. The third theorem only combines the other results. So no nontrivial reasoning is repeated across two proofs in the file.

The additivity theorem does repeat the structure of the Mathlib ball lemma, as its comment says: the same eight `set` integrals, `hI₁`, `hI₂`, `hI₀`, and the final `grind [wedgeIntegral]`. That repetition is cross-library. A shared convex-set lemma would have to take the rectangle-corner membership as hypotheses, because a ball does not contain the corners automatically. It would also have to change Mathlib's proof, which I can't edit from this library. I can't show both rewritten uses under the actual imports, and the target's version is already specialized: it uses `convex_halfSpace_im_gt` and positivity of the imaginary part. So I did not report a finding. The remaining uncertainty is whether upstream would want a convex-set generalization of the Mathlib lemma. That is outside what this rubric can justify here.
